creator: Alexander Terp
description: Left open by MIP-9's offered answers, 2026-10-25. The daemon decides who may answer a question by comparing names exactly; the core reads the human loosely. They agree in every case the shared table corpus/conformance/participant-names.json holds, which gives the human as the group's home names it (@human, or @human@laptop in a group kept elsewhere). They differ on one: @human@laptop asking in a group whose home calls the human @human (the core says it is not asked of the human, the daemon says it is). Settle how the human is named on a replica, then add the case. Related: the shell still re-derives whether a group is kept elsewhere (LinkPolicy.keptElsewhere) where the wire could say it.
title: How is the human spelled across machines, for who may answer a question?
